label: Teltonika RUTC40
description: An edge router with on-site compute: 1 WAN + 4 LAN at gigabit, a 4G modem, and enough CPU and storage to run containers at the branch rather than shipping every reading to a data centre.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUTC40 datasheet: 1 x WAN port 10/100/1000 Mbps and 4 x LAN ports 10/100/1000 Mbps (IEEE 802.3); 4G LTE modem. The datasheet states '4G' without naming the LTE category, so the cellular interface is modelled at the 100 Mbps Cat 4 class that every 4G model in this catalogue shares, and the note says so rather than implying a measured figure.

label: Teltonika RUTC42
description: A dual-modem edge router built for uptime: 1 WAN + 4 LAN at gigabit and two LTE Cat 4 modems, so a single carrier outage does not take the site down.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUTC42 datasheet: 1 x WAN port 10/100/1000 Mbps and 4 x LAN ports 10/100/1000 Mbps; two LTE Cat 4 modems, each rated up to 150 Mbps down / 50 Mbps up, so both cellular interfaces are modelled at 150M. Two wwan interfaces are modelled because redundancy is the entire reason to buy this model.

label: Teltonika RUTC50
description: An industrial 5G edge router: five gigabit ports (1 WAN + 4 LAN), WiFi 6, dual SIM and GPS, with on-site compute. The 5G modem is the point - 2.4-3.4 Gbps downlink against the 150 Mbps of the Cat 4 units.
notes: Vendor figures from the RUTC50 datasheet and wiki summary: 1 x WAN port 10/100/1000 Mbps, 4 x LAN ports 10/100/1000 Mbps (five gigabit ports total); WiFi 6; 5G Sub-6 GHz SA/NSA at 2.4-3.4 Gbps downlink with 4x4 MIMO; dual SIM; GPS. The cellular interface is modelled at the conservative 2.4 Gbps end of the vendor's downlink range rather than the 3.4 Gbps best case. The Wi-Fi interfaces are modelled at the standard WiFi 6 2x2 rates (574M on 2.4 GHz, 1.2G on 5 GHz) because the datasheet names WiFi 6 without quoting a client rate - if that matters for your lab, the radio standard is the quotable fact and the rate is the convention.
